habitats: Sheltered freshwater seeps on cooled young lava
summary: A 0.1–0.3 m photosynthetic rosette with sticky red-veined traps. Insects supplement mineral nutrition on seep-fed young lava. Scent works best in sheltered dawn air; sustained wind or rain makes trapping ineffective. The species does not occupy rich meadow soils (F7, F9, F16, F24, F25).

links: Seep-fed lava cracks provide water but little developed soil.
Photosynthesis supplies carbon while mineral nutrients remain scarce.
Mucilage captures small insects and digestive secretions release nutrients.
Absorption supplements nitrogen and phosphorus supply.
chains.play: Inspect captures to understand why the plant occupies damp bare-rock fissures.
chains.weakness: Sustained wind dries or fouls droplets, and sustained rain dilutes or washes them away; traps become ineffective until suitable conditions and secretions return.
observe: Fresh droplets stand on sheltered leaves.
Small insects stick while large visitors escape.
After prolonged rain, washed traps hold few new captures.

plausibility.summary: Carnivory supplements nutrients rather than replacing photosynthesis. Restrict plants to seep-fed nutrient-poor cooled lava; sustained wind and rain suppress effective capture.

analogues.mechanism: Prey-derived nutrients can offset the costs of traps in nutrient-poor habitats.

links: Trap secretions provide nearby insects with a food-like scent cue.
Still sheltered air allows the cue to persist.
Red veins mark defended foliage while specialists exploit trapped prey.
chains.play: Find active traps at still dawn and watch acechalunas steal captured insects.
chains.weakness: Sustained wind disrupts scent and capture; sustained rain dilutes secretions. Prey theft further reduces nutrient return.
observe: Insects approach during a still dawn interval.
Red veins remain beneath clear secretions.
Acechalunas removes prey without swallowing leaves.

plausibility.summary: Warning veins indicate alkaloids. Trapping is effective only during suitable sheltered intervals; persistent seep moisture does not protect aerial traps from wind or rain.

analogues.mechanism: Secretory traps incur construction and maintenance costs; the scent timing and warning pattern are fictional specializations.

food_for: Specialist omnivores taking small self-medication samples

poison.signal: Red veins warn of alkaloid-rich tissue and mucilage.

gameplay.notes: Merodeador sampling does not establish a safe player remedy. Traps cannot restrain creatures. Disable effective capture during sustained wind or rain; plants remain confined to seep-fed young lava rather than meadow soil.

relations.note: Occasionally samples defended foliage for established self-medication.
Steals small trapped insects, reducing plant nutrient return.
Occurs beside crust margins where fresh seepage reaches cooled lava.
Shares damp fissures; growing tussocks can shade rosettes.
Demonstrates defended foliage and nutrient-poor seep habitat.

generator.trunk: Short ground-hugging crown in a damp fissure.

branching.buttress: None; fine roots occupy existing cracks.

leaf.type: Fleshy tongue-shaped blade with stalked glands

overlay_rules: Clear droplets reflect ambient light without glowing.
Old prey remains form sparse brown flecks.
Sustained rain washes down droplets; sustained wind dries or fouls them.

placement.slope: Sheltered seep-fed ledges and fissures on stable cooled young lava.
placement.wetness: Persistent thin freshwater seepage without prolonged submersion.
placement.soil: Shallow nutrient-poor volcanic grit; exclude meadow loam, rich humus and hot vent crust.
placement.fog: Dawn humidity reduces drying; sufficient daylight remains necessary.
placement.density: Small colonies restricted to individual seep lines and sheltered cracks.

generator.seasonal: Expands traps while seepage persists; contracts toward the crown when water supply weakens. Capture resumes after weather damage only when secretions recover.
generator.wind_response: Low leaves remain attached, but sustained wind dries scent-bearing droplets and makes trapping ineffective.

journal.en: Sticky tongues drink the seep and catch insects. Red veins warn against a mouthful.
journal.es: Lenguas pegajosas beben del rezume y atrapan insectos. Las venas rojas advierten antes del bocado.

observe: Find sticky rosettes along damp cracks in bare lava.

secrets: Frequent acechalunas visits can empty apparently productive traps.
A surviving contracted crown can mark a seep temporarily withdrawn below the rock.
